hero.name: David Alejandro Fuquen Flórez
hero.bio: Software Engineer at Canals AI, a fast-growing U.S.-based AI startup for the industrial supply chain. Research and teaching experience across four countries: AI and robotics education research with Cornell University, a machine-learning hackathon at The University of Hong Kong's Shanghai campus with the CETIC Foundation, and an exchange at Politecnico di Milano. Adjunct Lecturer and Cum Laude graduate in Systems and Computing Engineering, with a minor in Physics, from Universidad de los Andes.

res1.title: Technical Advisor and Hackathon Lead, Orbit Odyssey
res1.subtitle: Cornell Cup Robotics, with The University of Hong Kong and the CETIC Foundation
res1.brief: Designed and co-built the computer vision challenge for the MeckUp Hackathon in Shanghai, with 100+ students aged 10-15 from across China.
res1.details:
Supervisor: Prof. David Schneider, Ph.D., Director of the Systems Engineering Program and Professor of Practice, Cornell University.

Designed and co-built the computer vision challenge for the <meckup>MeckUp Hackathon</meckup> at The University of Hong Kong's Zhangjiang Base in Shanghai (Aug 2026), with 100+ students aged 10-15 from across China.

Worked with Match Wai Lun Ko, Assistant Dean at The University of Hong Kong, and Lena Foo, Managing Principal of the <cetic>CETIC Foundation</cetic>, to design and run the challenge.

Co-built a web platform (FastAPI, Vue 3, Docker, Nginx) where teams trained and ran their own YOLO object detectors on a dedicated GPU server, giving every team identical resources, streaming live training metrics over WebSocket, and verifying submitted models with SHA-256 hashes.

Co-built the robot pipeline: YOLO models exported to ONNX on an Intel AIxBoard stream detections over UART to an XRP robot (MicroPython) that autonomously contacts or avoids objects.

Extended the platform with an NLP challenge (PyTorch intent classification and slot extraction) that teaches students to turn natural-language commands into robot actions, to be featured at the next MeckUp competition in Shanghai (Feb 2027).

Supervisor: Prof. Clifford Whitcomb, Ph.D., Director of Graduate Studies and Executive Director of the Systems Engineering Program, Cornell University.

Developed XRP robot features and an educational guide for Cornell SYSEN 5920 and 5100, the first program recognized by INCOSE as a knowledge-exam equivalent.

Contributed to the <xrp>XRP robotics education platform</xrp> by developing new features and improving the user experience, used in 180+ countries with partners including FIRST, Raspberry Pi, SparkFun, NASA, and Lockheed Martin.

Designed and built the GUI (React, Web Serial API, Python) and USB serial communication protocol for <agxrp>AgXRP</agxrp>, an open-source autonomous platform for precision agriculture, with robot-side control in MicroPython, supervised by Jonathan Jaramillo, Ph.D., Lecturer.

work1.title: Software Engineer, Accounts Payable
work1.subtitle: Canals AI
work1.brief: Develop Canals' AI-powered Accounts Payable product, built on LLM pipelines that read vendor invoices and submit them into distributors' ERPs.
work1.details:
Canals AI is a fast-growing U.S.-based AI startup (Coral Gables, FL; remote) that automates order processing and accounts payable for industrial wholesale distributors.

Develop Canals' AI-powered Accounts Payable product, whose LLM pipelines split each vendor invoice into multiple targeted model queries to extract its parts, match them to purchase orders, and submit payables into distributors' ERPs (Eclipse, Infor, P21).

Built a secure passwordless review flow for external users, such as customers' approvers without a Canals account, to approve, reject, or comment on expense invoices directly from an email link, using signed links, one-time email codes, device trust, and reCAPTCHA, while reusing the same review interface as logged-in users (TypeScript, PostgreSQL, Svelte).

Extended a customer-configurable rules engine that flags, routes, or blocks AI-processed invoices, adding new exception checks end to end, from backend detection to the settings UI.

Handled 150+ inbound customer tickets, diagnosing and resolving issues reported by distributors.

pub2.title: Recreating the V-JEPA 2-AC Architecture for Self-Supervised Video Models
pub2.subtitle: Séneca Repositorio Institucional - Universidad de los Andes
pub2.details:
Undergraduate thesis, advised by Prof. Rubén Manrique, Ph.D. Available <thesis>here</thesis>.

This project recreates the V-JEPA 2-AC architecture to better understand its self-supervised video learning and action-conditioned prediction capabilities. By analyzing the official Meta implementation, a fully functional local reproduction of both the pretraining and post-training stages was developed, along with a simplified variant of the post-training predictor.

Using a curated 206-video robotic dataset, all architectures were evaluated on their ability to infer plausible next actions from an initial and a goal frame. The results illustrate the feasibility of reproducing V-JEPA 2-AC locally, highlight the trade-offs introduced by simplification, and provide insight into how energy-based prediction landscapes guide robotic action selection.
